text.content: Princes rule through the Lextalionis, the vampire law laid down by Caine and described in the Traditions. It is rooted in Biblical tradition: "An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth." Those who break the law are slain, though with Lextalionis a prince may instead strip a Cainite of domain, exile him, or order his destruction for the most grievous offenses. Any Cainite may invoke Lextalionis to air a grievance, but only the prince can enforce it. A prince who abuses Lextalionis may find herself victim of her own punishments, so she must walk a fine line between strict justice and leniency. It is the privilege of the prince to decide how strictly she will interpret the law, what constitutes an offense, the guilt of the accused, and the style and severity of punishment.

The blood hunt is a death sentence that few escape. The prince must formally announce the hunt, and the accused has until midnight to leave the city. Once the hunt is called, any vampire may hunt and destroy the accused, though the sheriff typically leads the hunt. Some princes offer rewards to the vampire who destroys the offender, and choice prizes such as domain can inspire the formation of a lynch mob. Regardless of her actual guilt, the accused vampire will find very few willing to help her. Anyone caught aiding and abetting the fugitive is considered an accomplice and will likewise be hunted.

Blood hunts are traditionally called only in extreme cases, since once called, they cannot be stopped. Political enemies are the most common targets, but anyone who crosses the prince may find herself targeted.

Branding

Minor infractions (theft, or trespassing in another's domain) are punished with branding, which marks the crime visibly to all. The guilty party receives a mark burned into the face, arms, or somewhere visible, which is then rubbed with salt to slow its healing. A severe infraction might see the brand reapplied every few weeks to prevent it from fully healing.

Exile

Some crimes are not serious enough to warrant a blood hunt, but serious enough to deny the Cainite the protection of the city and its prince. Such vampires, called Autarkis, are branded and cast out of the domain. Without rights or protection, an Autarkis is considered fair game for hunting; some fall prey to Lupines while trying to survive in the wild, while the luckiest find their way to bands of outlaws called the Furores.

Ordeals

An ordeal, borrowed from mortal society, allows a prince to let the offending Cainite attempt to prove her innocence by enduring a challenge. Most ordeals are designed to be more entertaining to the court than fair to the Cainite on trial - innocence rarely plays a part in Cainite ordeals, whatever mortal society may believe about divine grace protecting the innocent. Common types include:

  • Trial by combat - frequently reserved for princes and elders.
  • Ordeal by fire - running a ring lit by a blazing fire, or being forced to walk across hot coals.
  • Test of the Beast - being hung in a cage and denied sustenance; those who frenzy are destroyed.
  • Partaking of light - being forced to endure the rising sun for a set period.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter One: Introduction and Setting
